note: quince#273, ruled 2026-07-30: a newly filed issue entered NO watch. `fetch_issues` reads only what was DECLARED or REFERENCED by an open PR, and an issue is neither at the moment it is filed — so the channel the gap protocol makes the RULING channel was the one channel with no wake. Measured: quince#265 landed on the architect's own quince#230 ruling and reached that seat only because the Operator asked by hand. THE BASELINE IS A HIGHWATER MARK, not a set diff: GitHub allocates issue and PR numbers monotonically from one sequence, so `new` is exactly `numbered above the highest seen`, which is correct under ANY window — where diffing a bounded list would be a silent cap, the thing `fetch_issues` refuses one function up. Here `before.issues.highwater` is 273 and the scan returns 282, 279, 274 and two older ones; only the three above the mark are news. THE TWO OLDER NUMBERS ARE THE CONTROL: a version that emitted one event per scanned issue, or that ignored the mark, would emit five and this fixture would fail. `issue-new` carries NO actor and NO label, deliberately — both filters were ruled out, because the implementer and supervisor seats file under one App identity (quince#227) so an author filter would swallow supervisor-filed ruling requests, and a label filter re-creates the declared-set problem one field over. Note that 270 is DECLARED and already in items: it must NOT produce an `issue-new`, because it is not new — it is merely still open, which is what distinguishes this event from `issue-first-observation`.
